title: [RAWTHROW][4] c10/util: four named files instead of a directory
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #194379
* #194378
* #194245
* #194244

## Author Notes

The main TORCH_CHECK macro itself is here.
Fix C++ test to catch the proper C++ errors.
Also allowlist vendored code. And skip two files that would have user-visible side effects.
The rest here is mechanical no-op moves.

## Agent Notes

Written by Claude Code:

> `c10/util/**` is 30 findings. Unlike the earlier phases it cannot be cleared, so
> the directory exclude becomes four named files instead - and the interesting
> part is which four.
>
> Six conversions, none of which changes what Python sees - though only one is
> actually reachable from Python, which is worth being precise about rather than
> hand-waving. `TypeCast.cpp`'s `report_overflow` is the live path, and the Test
> Plan below exercises it. `safe_conv.cpp`, `DynamicCounter.cpp` and
> `sparse_bitset.h` have no Python caller at all. `Registry.h`'s throw is gated on
> `terminate_`, which defaults to true, so a duplicate registration in any real
> build calls `std::exit(1)` and never reaches the throw; the single
> `SetTerminate(false)` in the tree is in `c10/test/util/registry_test.cpp`,
> immediately above the assertion this commit updates. For the five non-live
> sites the claim is that they would still be RuntimeError if they ever reached a
> binding. The six:
> `DynamicCounter.cpp`, `Registry.h`, `TypeCast.cpp`, `safe_conv.cpp`, and the two
> "Illegal empty element" throws in `sparse_bitset.h`. The comment in TypeCast.cpp
> explaining why the type was runtime_error rather than domain_error (issue 33562)
> is kept, since c10::Error lands on RuntimeError for the same reason.
> DynamicCounter's `std::logic_error` becomes c10::Error, the same departure from
> the plan's carve-out that the long-tail PR documented: logic_error surfaces as
> RuntimeError on both binding paths, so nothing observable changes.
>
> Nine throws are annotated rather than converted, for two reasons. Five are the
> error machinery itself, so converting them would be circular: the two
> `torchCheckFail` overloads every TORCH_CHECK routes through, `C10_THROW_ERROR`,
> and the two STANDALONE_TORCH_HEADER TORCH_CHECK definitions - which deliberately
> throw `std::runtime_error` and do not route through `torchCheckFail` at all. The
> other four are in Logging.cpp and already throw c10 types; there the reason is
> that they carry a captured source location and condition that no TORCH_CHECK
> form can express. Those four are `ThrowEnforceNotMet` and
> `ThrowEnforceFiniteNotMet` (the CAFFE_ENFORCE throw sites) plus two definitions
> of `MessageLogger::DealWithFatal`, which serve the glog-shim `CHECK_*` /
> `TORCH_CHECK_OP` family. The DealWithFatal pair are not overloads but the same
> signature under `#ifdef C10_USE_GLOG` and its `#else`, so only three of the four
> compile in any one build; the linter counts both because it is a text scanner.
> The three
> stale file-level `allow-raw-throw` markers on Exception.cpp, Exception.h and
> Logging.cpp are removed; they have licensed nothing since markers became
> line-scoped, and each was itself an orphaned-marker violation the exclude hid.
>
> Registry.h's new `Exception.h` include goes in the file's c10 block rather than
> the std block it would otherwise have inherited from the `<stdexcept>` it
> replaces, and the neighbouring comment about avoiding glog at static-init time
> gains a clause noting that plain TORCH_CHECK does not reintroduce that
> dependency - TORCH_CHECK_EQ lives in the same header, so the distinction is the
> expansion, not the include: TORCH_CHECK reaches `torchCheckFail`, while
> TORCH_CHECK_EQ goes through TORCH_CHECK_OP and NON_FATAL_IF to MessageLogger.
> The include is not free, though: Registry.h did not reach Exception.h before, so
> its TUs now also pull `<sstream>` and `<ostream>`. Compile time only, and the
> dominant consumer path (Logging.h to Flags.h to Registry.h) already had it.
>
> Two smaller things ride along. DynamicCounter's insert is hoisted into a named
> `inserted` local instead of being evaluated inside the TORCH_CHECK condition, so
> the state mutation is visible rather than buried in a check macro. TORCH_CHECK
> stringizes its condition under STRIP_ERROR_MESSAGES, so this also shortens that
> build's message from the whole insert expression to `inserted`. And two
> `NOLINTNEXTLINE(modernize-use-designated-initializers)` comments in
> Exception.cpp are deleted rather than moved to trailing position:
> `.clang-tidy` disables that check repo-wide, so they were already inert and
> nothing in OSS CI depended on them.
>
> `safe_conv_test.cpp` also drops an `#include <stdexcept>` that the retyping
> orphaned.
>
> Sixteen gtest assertions are updated from `std::runtime_error` to `c10::Error`,
> in safe_conv_test, Scalar_test, registry_test, scalar_test and pow_test.
> `c10::Error` derives from `std::exception`, not `std::runtime_error`, so every
> one of those would have failed once the converted paths started throwing it -
> demonstrated below rather than assumed. `c10::Error` is what the 53 assertions
> already in those directories expect; the count goes to 69. (A line-based grep says 50 and 66 - three pre-existing assertions wrap
> `c10::Error)` onto a continuation line, in legacy_vmap_test and
> DispatchKeySet_test. The +16 is the same either way.)
>
> Three observable differences are worth naming. First, under
> `TORCH_SHOW_CPP_STACKTRACES=1` the translator reports `what()` instead of
> `what_without_backtrace()` (torch/csrc/Exceptions.h), and
> `c10::Error::what()` carries a C++ backtrace - unconditionally for anything
> TORCH_CHECK throws, since that constructor always builds one - where
> `std::runtime_error::what()` returned the bare message - the flag selects the
> accessor, it does not change what c10 builds. That is the
> behaviour every existing TORCH_CHECK already has, and the flag is opt-in, so it
> is not a regression - but two Dynamo tests compared a hardcoded message string
> against `str(e)` from the converted overflow path, which only matched while the
> flag was off. `test/dynamo/test_nb_int.py` and `test_nb_float.py` now compare
> first lines. This is not hypothetical: `test/run_test.py:898` sets the flag when
> it retries a single test, so any flake in those files would have turned into a
> permanent retry failure.
>
> Second, under `-DSTRIP_ERROR_MESSAGES` (buckbuild.bzl, mobile custom builds)
> TORCH_CHECK_MSG collapses to the stringized condition and file, dropping the
> message. The exact shape is uglier than it looks - `#type` stringizes an empty
> `""` and C10_STRINGIZE re-quotes an already-quoted `__FILE__` - so it is
> literally:
>
>     false"" CHECK FAILED at "../c10/util/TypeCast.cpp"
>
> for five of the six converted sites, and `inserted"" CHECK FAILED at ...` for
> DynamicCounter, whose condition is now a named local. All six lose their message
> text in those builds where the raw throw preserved it.
>
> Two test knock-ons in such a build, both latent because mobile and custom builds
> run neither suite: the two Dynamo assertions below would fail, since eager
> collapses to that string while Dynamo's synthesized literal does not; and
> `test/cpp/api/tensor.cpp:721,726` assert on the `report_overflow` text, so they
> would too. Those two are the only in-tree assertions on a converted message
> outside the five edited test files, and they pass today because
> ASSERT_THROWS_WITH catches `c10::Error` by name and uses
> what_without_backtrace(). Again this is what every existing TORCH_CHECK already
> does, but it is a real difference and not worth claiming away.
>
> Third, and this is the one with teeth in C++ rather than Python: `c10::Error`
> derives from `std::exception`, not `std::runtime_error`, so a
> `catch (const std::runtime_error&)` around any converted site stops firing.
> That is exactly why the 16 gtest assertions below had to change. No in-tree
> non-test catch site is affected - I grepped `catch (const std::runtime_error&)`
> and the logic_error equivalent across every tracked C/C++/ObjC++ file, matching
> across line breaks and both const spellings. Seventeen sites; the five in tests
> and benchmarks catch exceptions those files raise themselves, and none of the
> twelve non-test ones can reach a converted function. The only `.mm` one,
> `PTMCoreMLCompiler.mm:100`, is iOS-only and unrelated. The closest call
> is `aten/src/ATen/native/sparse/SparseBlasImpl.cpp:250`, a non-test
> `catch (std::runtime_error&)` that exists to catch pybind's `py::cast_error`;
> that still derives from `std::runtime_error` so it keeps working, and I could
> not construct a path where a converted site throws underneath it. Out-of-tree
> extensions and custom ops catching these by base class get no such patch.
>
> What stays excluded splits two ways. Permanent:
>
>     c10/util/flat_hash_map.h      skarupke/flat_hash_map. Vendored then patched
>                                   - 23 in-tree commits, including a real fix in
>                                   #181037 - so the reason is that we still track
>                                   upstream's shape, not that the file is
>                                   untouched.
>     c10/util/order_preserving_flat_hash_map.h
>                                   The same skarupke upstream, forked at a pinned
>                                   commit and modified to preserve insertion
>                                   order. Permanent for a second, independent
>                                   reason: at()'s std::out_of_range is caught by
>                                   name and turned into KeyError in
>                                   torch/csrc/jit/python/python_dict.cpp, so
>                                   converting it would silently break TorchScript
>                                   dicts.
>
> Deferred to phase 9, because converting them is a behaviour change:
>
>     c10/util/SmallVector.cpp      Being LLVM ADT is not the whole reason. The 2
>                                   length_error are upstream's own, documented in
>                                   the preserved doc comments, but the 3 bad_alloc
>                                   are PyTorch's, replacing llvm::safe_malloc and
>                                   safe_realloc - so "vendored" does not cover
>                                   them. The operative reason is that pybind11 maps
>                                   bad_alloc to MemoryError and the 2
>                                   length_error to ValueError
>                                   (detail/internals.h translate_exception),
>                                   neither of which c10::Error can produce.
>     c10/util/StringUtil.cpp       std::range_error -> ValueError, same shape.
>
> `sparse_bitset.h` looks like a third: it carries LLVM's license header. But both
> throws are ours, not LLVM's: upstream ends both functions with
> `llvm_unreachable("Illegal empty element")`, and the copy imported in #20899
> already had the throw substituted, so git alone will not show the swap. Either
> way the throw is code we maintain, and excluding the file would have permanently
> exempted it. It is converted, and
> both sites reach Python as RuntimeError before and after - they are inside
> TorchScript's liveness / alias analysis, not a binding boundary.
>
> StringUtil's three `std::range_error` come from UTF-16 surrogate decoding in the
> `#ifndef _WIN32` branch - so this configuration is the one that compiles them,
> and the Windows path goes through `u16u8` instead. A bare pybind11 binding turns
> range_error into ValueError, and CATCH_CORE_ERRORS has no std::exception arm to
> intercept it first. In-tree, four tests in `c10/test/util/string_util_test.cpp`
> pass wide strings through `c10::str`, and `aten/src/ATen/MapAllocator.cpp` puts
> `const wchar_t*` into TORCH_CHECK - but the tests all pass valid UTF-16 and
> MapAllocator's uses are inside `#ifdef _WIN32`, which takes the `u16u8` path
> instead. So the throws stay unreached, but "unreached today" is not a good
> enough reason to change an exception type in a mechanical PR.
>
> Test Plan:
>
> ```
> bash -ic 'BUILD_CONFIG spin develop'
> ```
>
> Builds clean - a wide rebuild, since Exception.h and Registry.h are included
> almost everywhere.
>
> ```
> python -m pytest -q test/test_torch.py test/test_type_promotion.py test/test_autograd.py
> ```
>
> 2085 passed, 129 skipped. The one failure, `test_qengine`, is pre-existing: this
> configuration sets USE_FBGEMM=0 and USE_QNNPACK=0, so
> `torch.backends.quantized.supported_engines` is empty.
>
> The converted overflow path checked against the built torch, since it is the one
> users actually reach:
>
> ```
> torch.zeros(2, dtype=torch.uint8).fill_(100000)
>     RuntimeError: value cannot be converted to type uint8_t without overflow
> torch.tensor(2**40, dtype=torch.int32)
>     RuntimeError: value cannot be converted to type int32 without overflow
> ```
>
> Same type and same message as before. `report_narrowing_overflow` has no Python
> caller, so both of its branches were checked by linking c10 directly:
>
> ```
> g++ -std=c++17 -I. -Ibuild -Itorch/include probe.cpp -Lbuild/lib -lc10
>     [value cannot be safely converted without overflow]
>     [value cannot be safely converted without overflow: int8_t]
> ```
>
> The `ostringstream` bodies in TypeCast.cpp and safe_conv.cpp are deliberately
> left alone. Passing the pieces as TORCH_CHECK varargs would match
> DynamicCounter, but under STRIP_ERROR_MESSAGES the macro discards its varargs,
> leaving `name` unused and tripping -Wunused-parameter. Both are cold
> `[[noreturn]]` paths, so there is nothing to win by churning them here.
>
> ```
> lintrunner --take RAWTHROW --all-files
> ```
>
> Clean. Scoped to the directory this PR is about, since the repo-wide number
> depends on which globs you sweep:
>
> ```
> python tools/linter/adapters/raw_throw_linter.py $(git ls-files 'c10/util/*.cpp' 'c10/util/*.h')
> ```
>
> 30 findings before, 12 after. The 18 removed reconcile exactly to the diff: 6
> conversions, 9 annotations, and the 3 stale file-level markers, each of which
> was itself an orphaned-marker finding. The 12 that remain in c10/util are all
> inside the four excluded files. The exclude list goes from 8 entries to
> 11, which is the direction that matters here: a directory covering 157 tracked
> .cpp/.h files becomes four named ones - two permanent, two waiting on phase 9.
>
> `sparse_bitset.h` is header-only, so its two converted sites only compile where
> the enclosing template members are instantiated. It does have local consumers -
> `torch/csrc/jit/passes/liveness.h` and `passes/utils/memory_dag.h` include it -
> but only `find_first` is reached from there, so `find_last` was forced by hand:
>
> ```
> g++ -std=c++17 -fsyntax-only -Werror -I. -Ibuild -Itorch/include -xc++ - <<'EOF'
> #include <c10/util/sparse_bitset.h>
> int probe(const c10::SparseBitVectorElement<128>& e) {
>   return e.find_first() + e.find_last();
> }
> EOF
> ```
>
> The Dynamo edits were checked under both settings of the flag they exist for:
>
> ```
> TORCH_SHOW_CPP_STACKTRACES={0,1} pytest -q test/dynamo/test_nb_float.py
>     30 passed, both ways
> PYTHONPATH=<_testcapi stub> TORCH_SHOW_CPP_STACKTRACES={0,1} \
>     pytest -q test/dynamo/test_nb_int.py -k test_tensor_complex_raises
>     1 passed, both ways
> ```
>
> `test_nb_int.py` needs the stub because its line 4 does
> `from _testcapi import instancemethod` at module scope and this venv's CPython
> lacks that module, so the whole file fails collection. That gap is pre-existing
> and unrelated - it came in with fc65eec07dc - and stubbing the one symbol is
> enough to run the real assertion rather than a reconstruction of it.
>
> BUILD_TEST=0 in this configuration, but that only stops cmake building the gtest
> targets - the five changed test files can be compiled and run directly against
> the built libraries, so the 16 updated assertions did not have to be left to CI:
>
> ```
> g++ -std=c++17 -I. -Ibuild -Ithird_party/googletest/googletest/include \
>     <test>.cpp gtest-all.o gtest_main.o -Lbuild/lib -lc10 [-ltorch_cpu]
> ```
>
>     safe_conv_test              8 tests passed
>     registry_test               3 tests passed
>     c10 Scalar_test             3 tests passed
>     ATen scalar_test            4 tests passed   (needs -std=c++20)
>     pow_test                   13 tests passed   (needs -std=c++20)
>
> registry_test is the interesting one: `RegistryPriorities` is the only caller in
> the tree that reaches Registry.h's converted throw at all, so the one site with
> no production path is the one with direct coverage.
>
> As a positive control, rebuilding safe_conv_test with the old
> `std::runtime_error` expectation fails 6 of its 8 tests, which is the retyping
> being necessary rather than merely asserted.
>
> Left to CI: CLANGTIDY, and the changed .cpp files under CI's bare `-Werror`.
